passages.title: Passage I (Questions 101–105)
passages.body:
All such organisms as plants, animals, microorganisms and human beings as well as the physical surroundings interact with each other and maintain a balance in nature. All the interacting organisms in an area together with the non-living constituents of the environment form an ecosystem. Thus, an ecosystem consists of biotic components comprising living organisms and abiotic components comprising physical factors like temperature, rainfall, wind, soil and minerals.

For example, if you visit a garden you will find different plants, such as grasses, trees; flower-bearing plants like rose, jasmine, sunflower; and animals like frogs, insects and birds. All these living organisms interact with each other and their growth, reproduction and other activities are affected by the abiotic components of the ecosystem. So a garden is an ecosystem. Other types of ecosystems are forests, ponds and lakes. These are natural ecosystems while gardens and crop-fields are human-made ecosystems.
passages.source: CDS I 2022 English set A (set code GHSA-U-ENG – A)

passages.title: Passage II (Questions 106–110)
passages.body:
As we discussed food and sang every song we could remember and talked incessantly, we were slowly moving deeper into the Atlantic, and we got the feeling, really, that we belonged there, and that the ships that passed on the horizon were only hurrying strangers. We were actually living on the ocean. We discovered that the birds all seemed to league up at night-time, resting on the water by the hundreds. When we came poking along, we seemed so much a part of the sea that the birds wouldn't move until we were about five yards away. Then they'd flutter off, leaving feathers floating in the water, and settle again a few yards away.

The dolphins and porpoises would come up at sunset and move in among us and the birds. They'd come up very lazily under the birds, which would go up on their heels and flap their wings a bit, and then settle right down again. Two whales joined us one evening and played ring-around-rosie so close to us that Chay could have reached out an oar and tapped one.

We had calculated that we had just enough rations to make England, but the easterly winds caused an agonizing reappraisal. It would have been an interesting experience, running right down like that, but we felt we must not risk other people's lives by making them search for us. We decided to accept rations from the next ship that stopped. Was it a mature decision?

This was also the time when the strain of the voyage really began to tell on us. I wrote in my log: ‘I have known fear many times in my life, and indeed I have often striven to develop a situation that provided fear in both boxing and parachuting. I have never known anything like this — cannot be over tomorrow, or for many tomorrows. Somehow it is like being rubbed down with sandpaper. I honestly do not know how many storms there have been now, and each leaves us progressively weaker.’

‘Tonight we lie and wait. Nothing could save us if we get into difficulties. No ship could get us off these seas even if it arrived in time. We are completely in God's hands, at the mercy of the weather. All night the wind screams louder and louder, and the sound of the sea grows. We talk of many things — the night train to Scotland, the many things we've done, and slowly we are overtaken by an enormous feeling of humility and a desire to return to try and live a better life. The weather reached a climax at 0300 and then declined rapidly. Thank goodness we could not see the sea.’
passages.source: CDS I 2022 English set A (set code GHSA-U-ENG – A)

passages.title: Cloze passage (Questions 71–80)
passages.body: Bad habits such as over-eating, drinking, or smoking (71) _____ very easy to acquire. One should fight (72) _____ the force of habit. Even good things can be very harmful when done (73) _____ excess. The wise man is conscious (74) _____ his bad habits and checks them promptly. The use of tobacco has spread all (75) _____ the world. Those who have acquired this bad habit would (76) _____ be able to get rid of it. Alcohol, which is more common in cold countries than in warmer ones, does nobody any good and should be avoided (77) _____ Alcohol, even if taken in small quantities, (78) _____ to affect one's health. For the victims of alcoholism, (79) _____ helps, but this condition cannot be cured. Symptoms of alcoholism include repeated alcohol consumption (80) _____ serious related legal and health issues.
passages.source: CDS I 2022 English set A (set code GHSA-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Find the part of the sentence that has an error. If there is no error, choose (d).

__This task is being undertaken__ (a) __for the benefit of young people in needed__ (b) __at the instance of the Chief of the Group.__ (c) No error. (d)
questions.explanation:
Concept: Spot the grammatical error.
Step 1: 'Young people in need' needs the noun 'need', not the participle 'needed'.
Step 2: Part (b) is wrong.
Answer: (b).
questions.source: CDS I 2022 English set A (set code GHSA-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Find the part of the sentence that has an error. If there is no error, choose (d).

__If I am__ (a) __the principal of the school__ (b) __I would abolish all examinations.__ (c) No error. (d)
questions.explanation:
Concept: Spot the grammatical error.
Step 1: 'I would abolish' shows an imaginary condition, so the 'if' clause needs 'were'.
Step 2: Part (a) is wrong.
Answer: (a).
questions.source: CDS I 2022 English set A (set code GHSA-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Find the part of the sentence that has an error. If there is no error, choose (d).

__My mother is thinking__ (a) __that I should__ (b) __stop drinking.__ (c) No error. (d)
questions.explanation:
Concept: Spot the grammatical error.
Step 1: 'Think' meaning 'believe' is not used in the continuous form.
Step 2: It should be 'My mother thinks that...'. Part (a) is wrong.
Answer: (a).
questions.source: CDS I 2022 English set A (set code GHSA-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Find the part of the sentence that has an error. If there is no error, choose (d).

__The students have__ (a) __a good time__ (b) __in the class today.__ (c) No error. (d)
questions.explanation:
Concept: Spot the grammatical error.
Step 1: The key treats the action as already over, so the past 'had a good time' is needed.
Step 2: Part (a) is wrong. Treat this item as low-confidence, since 'have' can describe a habit.
Answer: (a).
questions.source: CDS I 2022 English set A (set code GHSA-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Find the part of the sentence that has an error. If there is no error, choose (d).

__More than thirty lakh people__ (a) __were inoculated against COVID-19__ (b) __on March 15th.__ (c) No error. (d)
questions.explanation:
Concept: Spot the grammatical error.
Step 1: The plural subject takes 'were', and the date phrase is correct.
Step 2: There is no error.
Answer: (d).
questions.source: CDS I 2022 English set A (set code GHSA-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Find the part of the sentence that has an error. If there is no error, choose (d).

__LIC was found__ (a) __on September 1, 1956__ (b) __via the Life Insurance Corporation Act.__ (c) No error. (d)
questions.explanation:
Concept: Spot the grammatical error.
Step 1: 'Found' (past of 'find') is wrong here. The verb meaning 'establish' is 'found, founded, founded'.
Step 2: It should be 'LIC was founded'. Part (a) is wrong.
Answer: (a).
questions.source: CDS I 2022 English set A (set code GHSA-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Find the part of the sentence that has an error. If there is no error, choose (d).

__Full many a flower__ (a) __are born__ (b) __to blush unseen.__ (c) No error. (d)
questions.explanation:
Concept: Spot the grammatical error.
Step 1: 'Many a' is followed by a singular noun and a singular verb: 'many a flower is born'.
Step 2: Part (b) is wrong.
Answer: (b).
questions.source: CDS I 2022 English set A (set code GHSA-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Find the part of the sentence that has an error. If there is no error, choose (d).

__I shall be glad to help__ (a) __every one of my boys__ (b) __in their studies.__ (c) No error. (d)
questions.explanation:
Concept: Spot the grammatical error.
Step 1: 'Every one' is singular, so the pronoun should be 'his', not 'their'.
Step 2: Part (c) is wrong.
Answer: (c).

Answer: (d).

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:

__For most food park__ (a) __marketing initiatives are restricted to__ (b) __a few hundred kilometres.__ (c) No error. (d)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:

Fifteen years ______, Elizabeth left her career and moved to India with her spouse.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Choose the word that fits grammar and meaning.
Step 1: 'Fifteen years ago' counts back from now.
Step 2: 'Before' needs a reference point in the past, and 'since' needs a starting point.
Answer: (a).

Your attempt can hardly be called successful, for it ______ had no good results.

As per the existing market rate, twelve dozen ______ one hundred rupees.

Concept: Choose the word that fits grammar and meaning.
Step 1: 'Twelve dozen' is a plural amount, so the verb is 'cost'.
Step 2: 'Costed' is used only when working out prices.
Answer: (b).

questions.question:

questions.subject: Sentence Organisation
questions.topic: Ordering of Sentences in a Passage
questions.question:
Directions: S1 and S6 are fixed. Arrange P, Q, R and S in between so that the six sentences form a coherent passage.

S1: Hunger and malnutrition are outcomes of food insecurity or the inability to access adequate food and nutrition.
S6: It is most likely that India is going to miss the Millennium Development Goal in this regard.
P: In 2001-03, every fifth Indian was found to be undernourished.
Q: The rate of decline in the proportion of the undernourished through the 1990s was much slower in comparison to the decline in poverty headcount ratio.
R: Hunger-related poverty remains one of the major deprivations in India.
S: In fact, the proportion of undernourished people remained stagnant at 21% in the second half of 1990s, and the number actually increased.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Find the opening idea, then follow the links (this, also, however).
Step 1: R states the general point (hunger-related poverty), and P gives the 2001-03 figure.
Step 2: Q compares the slow decline with poverty, and S ('In fact') adds the stagnation, leading to S6.
Answer: (a) RPQS.
questions.source: CDS I 2022 English set A (set code GHSA-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Sentence Organisation
questions.topic: Ordering of Sentences in a Passage
questions.question:
Directions: S1 and S6 are fixed. Arrange P, Q, R and S in between so that the six sentences form a coherent passage.

S1: The Indian Meteorological Department (IMD) was established in 1975.
S6: These predictions have an effect on the Indian economy that belies any belief that the economy of our country is not solely dependent on agriculture and the rains that feed it.
P: The Meteorological Department is perhaps also burdened with the most critical form of soothsaying i.e., forecasting the monsoon.
Q: The Crop Yield Formation Unit of the department has developed statistical models using correlation and regression techniques.
R: The IMD issued the first operational long range forecast of seasonal south-west monsoon rainfall in India in 1986.
S: It is the natural meteorological service and the principal agency in all matters related to meteorology.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Find the opening idea, then follow the links (this, also, however).
Step 1: S ('It is the natural meteorological service') follows S1 and describes the IMD.
Step 2: R gives the first long-range forecast, Q the statistical models, and P the monsoon forecasting. 'These predictions' in S6 refers to them.
Answer: (b) SRQP.
questions.source: CDS I 2022 English set A (set code GHSA-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Sentence Organisation
questions.topic: Ordering of Sentences in a Passage
questions.question:
Directions: S1 and S6 are fixed. Arrange P, Q, R and S in between so that the six sentences form a coherent passage.

S1: Let us posit two questions: one, what ails our parliamentary system?
S6: Given the current political scenario, it appears that India has yet to develop a strong parliamentary culture.
P: To search for an answer, we begin with Rudolf’s observation that the parliamentary life has deteriorated in India.
Q: Two, how democratic is our democracy?
R: For a system to survive, grow and prosper, it needs to be supported by a democratic political culture.
S: There is an organic connectivity between a parliamentary system and parliamentary democracy.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Find the opening idea, then follow the links (this, also, however).
Step 1: Q ('Two, ...') directly follows S1 ('one, ...').
Step 2: P begins the search for an answer, R says what a system needs, and S links the parliamentary system to democracy, leading to S6.
Answer: (d) QPRS.
questions.source: CDS I 2022 English set A (set code GHSA-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Sentence Organisation
questions.topic: Ordering of Sentences in a Passage
questions.question:
Directions: S1 and S6 are fixed. Arrange P, Q, R and S in between so that the six sentences form a coherent passage.

S1: People of every country think very highly of themselves and consider their country the best or the greatest.

questions.source: CDS I 2022 English set A (set code GHSA-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Reading Comprehension
questions.question: Abiotic components of the ecosystem refer to
questions.explanation:
Concept: Use only what the passage says.
Step 1: The passage says abiotic components comprise 'physical factors like temperature, rainfall, wind, soil and minerals'.
Answer: (d).
questions.source: CDS I 2022 English set A (set code GHSA-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Reading Comprehension
questions.question: Which of the following is not a natural ecosystem?
questions.explanation:
Concept: Use only what the passage says.
Step 1: The passage says forests, ponds and lakes are natural, while gardens and crop-fields are human-made.
Answer: (a).
questions.source: CDS I 2022 English set A (set code GHSA-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Reading Comprehension
questions.question: The word ‘constituent’ in the passage implies
questions.explanation:
Concept: Use only what the passage says.
Step 1: 'Constituent' means a part of a whole, so 'component'.
Answer: (c).
questions.source: CDS I 2022 English set A (set code GHSA-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Reading Comprehension
questions.question: “We were actually living on the ocean,” implies
questions.opt_b: they were on a long voyage into the Atlantic.
questions.opt_c: they were without any source of income.
questions.opt_d: they were fishing deep into the Atlantic for their living.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Use only what the passage says.
Step 1: The sentence follows 'moving deeper into the Atlantic', so it means they were on a long sea voyage.
Answer: (b).
questions.source: CDS I 2022 English set A (set code GHSA-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Reading Comprehension
questions.question: “... the birds all seemed to league up at night-time,” implies
questions.explanation:
Concept: Use only what the passage says.
Step 1: The next clause says the birds rested 'by the hundreds', so 'league up' means come together.
Step 2: (d) is close, but UPSC's key is (c). Treat this item as low-confidence.
Answer: (c).
questions.source: CDS I 2022 English set A (set code GHSA-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Reading Comprehension
questions.question: What did the author write in his log?
questions.opt_a: They faced the worst kind of fear ever experienced.
questions.opt_b: They were excellent in boxing and parachuting.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Use only what the passage says.
Step 1: The log says 'I have never known anything like this', so they faced the worst fear of their lives.
Answer: (a).
questions.source: CDS I 2022 English set A (set code GHSA-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Reading Comprehension
questions.question: They lost all hope of survival because
questions.opt_b: there was no help coming to them.
questions.opt_c: they were facing a severe sea-storm.
questions.opt_d: they were frightened by the whales and dolphins.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Use only what the passage says.
Step 1: The log says 'Nothing could save us' and 'each storm leaves us weaker', so they faced a severe sea-storm.
Step 2: (b) is close, but UPSC's key is (c).
Answer: (c).
questions.source: CDS I 2022 English set A (set code GHSA-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Reading Comprehension
questions.question: “We are overtaken by an enormous feeling of humility,” implies that they
questions.opt_b: were ready to accept help from the ships around them.
questions.opt_c: needed equipment and food to survive.
questions.opt_d: have accepted the strength and power of nature with modesty.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Use only what the passage says.
Step 1: 'Humility' before the weather ('at the mercy of the weather') means accepting nature's power modestly.
Answer: (d).
questions.source: CDS I 2022 English set A (set code GHSA-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Find which part of speech the underlined word or phrase belongs to.

The conclusions that they came to are highly __questionable__.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Part of speech depends on the job a word does in the sentence.
Step 1: 'Questionable' describes 'conclusions', so it is an adjective.
Answer: (b).
questions.source: CDS I 2022 English set A (set code GHSA-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Find which part of speech the underlined word or phrase belongs to.

This year marks the __quincentenary__ of Columbus’s voyage to America.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Part of speech depends on the job a word does in the sentence.
Step 1: 'Quincentenary' names a 500th anniversary and follows 'the', so it is a noun.
Answer: (a).
questions.source: CDS I 2022 English set A (set code GHSA-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Find which part of speech the underlined word or phrase belongs to.

I still cherish the memories of those __far-off__ days.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Part of speech depends on the job a word does in the sentence.
Step 1: 'Far-off' describes 'days', so it is an adjective.
Answer: (c).
questions.source: CDS I 2022 English set A (set code GHSA-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Find which part of speech the underlined word or phrase belongs to.

I don’t think I’ll come on Saturday. I have a lot of work to do. __Besides__, I don’t really like parties.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Part of speech depends on the job a word does in the sentence.
Step 1: Here 'besides' means 'also' and links ideas without an object, so it is an adverb.
Answer: (b).
questions.source: CDS I 2022 English set A (set code GHSA-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Find which part of speech the underlined word or phrase belongs to.

The __bottomline__ is that we have to make a decision today.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Part of speech depends on the job a word does in the sentence.
Step 1: 'The bottomline' is the subject of the sentence, so it is a noun.
Answer: (a).
questions.source: CDS I 2022 English set A (set code GHSA-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Find which part of speech the underlined word or phrase belongs to.

Try to knock that vase __over__.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Part of speech depends on the job a word does in the sentence.
Step 1: 'Over' completes the verb 'knock' and has no object, so it is an adverb.
Answer: (d).
questions.source: CDS I 2022 English set A (set code GHSA-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Find which part of speech the underlined word or phrase belongs to.

I’d like an ice cream. Are you having __one__ too?
questions.explanation:
Concept: Part of speech depends on the job a word does in the sentence.
Step 1: 'One' stands in for 'an ice cream', so it is a pronoun.
Answer: (b).
questions.source: CDS I 2022 English set A (set code GHSA-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Find which part of speech the underlined word or phrase belongs to.

My parents lent me the money. __Otherwise__, I could not have afforded the trip.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Part of speech depends on the job a word does in the sentence.
Step 1: 'Otherwise' means 'if not' and links the two sentences as a conjunctive adverb.
Answer: (b).
questions.source: CDS I 2022 English set A (set code GHSA-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Find which part of speech the underlined word or phrase belongs to.

She wrote me an __anguished__ letter from her prison cell.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Part of speech depends on the job a word does in the sentence.
Step 1: 'Anguished' describes 'letter', so it is an adjective.
Answer: (c).
questions.source: CDS I 2022 English set A (set code GHSA-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Find which part of speech the underlined word or phrase belongs to.

There is __a__ visitor for you.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Part of speech depends on the job a word does in the sentence.
Step 1: 'A' is the indefinite article.
Answer: (c).
questions.source: CDS I 2022 English set A (set code GHSA-U-ENG – A)
